assumptions: 'Agents' means the two AI agents in the workspace; the only tools that matter are those in their tools lists
'Email customers' means util.send_email in a tool; no endpoint or task sends email
'Delete anything' means db.del, db.bulk.delete and db.truncate, reachable from a tool
Approval is modelled as a row in a new email_approvals table set to approved by a person; no approval UI or endpoint was built
Advisory, active policy, since the customer asked to prevent but the skill says blocking is the owner's choice
Key HITL-001 is my own; no template key fits
confusions: Policy path: the skill and brief say policies/<KEY>.xs, but xano policy parse resolved it relative to the current directory; I had to pass ./workspace/policies/HITL-001.xs. The first attempt used policies/HITL-001.xs from the project root and failed with ENOENT.

Recipe 'Keep AI calls affordable and agents safe' lists 'AI tools cannot delete records' and 'Deletes and emails wait for an approval check' together, with stack.statement_order after db.del. If tools cannot delete at all, the delete half of the approval rule never applies. The recipe does not say to drop it.

stack.statement_order's 'before' guard for the email: the skill says a guard written as conditional { throw } does not count. Whether a precondition inside a called function counts as a before at the call site is implied by the catalogue text but not stated as an example, so I relied on the catalogue text.

The 'Scope by' section lists object_kinds for tool, but the not-checkable section does not say whether a tool's own tools list (which tools an agent may expose) is out of reach; I inferred it from the 'Agent tool allowlists' entry.
The skill file preview was truncated at 430 lines and I had to read the rest in a second call; not a product issue but worth knowing for long skills.
wished_for: A worked example of a human-approval gate: one table, one function, one tool, and the two rules together
A check or param that limits which tools an agent may be given (the ask's second part)
A note in the recipe that deletes are forbidden in tools, so the 'before delete' half of the recipe is not needed for tools
A line in the catalogue saying precondition inside a called function counts for stack.statement_order before
parse_errors_seen: Policy parse failed: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'policies/HITL-001.xs' (wrong working directory; succeeded with ./workspace/policies/HITL-001.xs)
dry_run_problems_seen: None blocking. Dry run created 1 policy, 1 table, 1 function, updated 1 tool; no blocked objects or missing references reported.
Parse warning HITL-001.R2 (function not on branch) is expected for a function created in the same change; not a dry-run problem.
why_confidence: Deletes from tools are fully checked by statement_forbidden, including through called functions, so that half is high. Email is checked only for order: a tool that sends email must call require_human_approval first, and that function only blocks if its approval row is not approved. Whether anyone can approve rows is outside what a check can see. The 'tools I haven't given them' part has no check; it is not covered. The delete rule will flag the existing delete_customer_note tool, which I did not change. I did not run policy evaluate, so the findings the rules produce on this workspace are predictions only.
